android_mechanism: Packet-factory properties cache grows without bound; fix bounds the retained data
bug_description: The home article list is bound to PersistentStorage ('homeList'). Every load-more during infinite scrolling concatenates another page and rewrites the ENTIRE accumulated list (JSON serialization + preferences write) to disk, so persistent-storage write time and retained memory grow quadratically with scroll depth; the full tail is also re-parsed on every cold start even though it is stale feed data.
fix_summary: Only the first-page home-article snapshot is persisted ('homeListCache') for fast cold-start rendering; pages loaded during the session accumulate in component state without rewriting persistent storage.

test_oracle.definition: Pss of the app process after the workload, from the periodic smaps_rollup snapshots in memory/.
test_oracle.comparison: unfixed >= 1.2 * fixed over >= 3 rounds per variant

evidence.measured_as: perf_hw-instructions over the load-more persistence workload (Pura 70 Ultra)
evidence.note: 38.9M vs 4.56M median hw-instructions (8.5x, disjoint ranges, high unfixed variance); mechanism counter 284970 vs 5111 persisted bytes per load-more (measurements-staging).

mechanism_oracle.definition: Bytes written to app preferences/storage attributable to home-list persistence per load-more cycle, from disk/filesystem trace activity (write sizes grow with list length in unfixed, stay constant in fixed).
mechanism_oracle.comparison: unfixed: write size per load-more grows linearly with accumulated pages (total write volume quadratic in pages); fixed: writes only at first-page fetch. unfixed_total_write_bytes > fixed by >= 3x after 10 pages; unfixed resident memory higher.

reproduction: git -C hosts/wanharmony checkout case/wanharmony_persisted_home_list_growth/unfixed; apply the measurement harness patch for this case, build, sign and install the HAP.
git -C hosts/wanharmony checkout case/wanharmony_persisted_home_list_growth/fixed; rebuild, reinstall and repeat identically.
Compare test_oracle.metric across the two report sets: unfixed >= 1.2 * fixed.
